supporting_observations.claim: WINWORD.EXE opened C:\Users\maria.lopez\Downloads\Statement.docm under Maria Lopez's account shortly before the PowerShell activity.

Word spawned PowerShell with no-profile, hidden-window, and encoded-command options. The encoded command decodes to an expression that downloads and executes a string from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
PowerShell made a proxy request for the referenced u.ps1 URL; the proxy recorded a successful response.

PowerShell created a temporary file and then launched rundll32 with C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init. The rundll32 process ran under Maria Lopez's account and exited about 19 seconds after PowerShell started.

The sequence of a macro-enabled document opening, hidden encoded PowerShell downloading a script, and rundll32 invoking a DLL from the user's roaming profile is strongly indicative of malicious execution, rather than routine patching described in the environment context.

The hidden-window option is recorded, but the supplied telemetry does not establish what Maria saw on screen.
